misconceptions.description: Using satisfaction or attitude ratings as evidence that learning occurred
misconceptions.trigger: learner reports high satisfaction and concludes the module taught the skill
misconceptions.feedback: Satisfaction is a usability and attitude metric. Support a learning claim with a learning metric such as pre/post or transfer performance.

misconceptions.description: Pairing a claim with a metric that measures a different construct
misconceptions.trigger: learner backs a learning claim with a usability metric or vice versa
misconceptions.feedback: Match the metric to the construct: findability to task success or time, mastery to outcome scores, transfer to novel-item accuracy.

misconceptions.description: Collapsing distinct usability and learning metrics into one composite number
misconceptions.trigger: learner reports a single effectiveness score combining different constructs
misconceptions.feedback: Keep the metrics disaggregated so a reader can see which specific claim each result supports.

misconceptions.description: Treating an immediate post-test gain as evidence of durable or transferable learning
misconceptions.trigger: learner claims durable learning from a test taken right after the content was shown
misconceptions.feedback: Add a delay or a transfer item so the gain is not just short-term recall of just-seen answers.
